title: Markdown loads rejects a valid line whose title is one character and that has tags (round trip fails)
spec_quote: `loads(dumps(tasks)) == tasks` for normalized tasks. / Lines that are empty are ignored on load; any other line that does not have this shape raises `TaskError`.
probe_note: t = [normalize({id:1, title:'X', tags:['home'], created:'2026-01-01'})]; fmt_md.loads(fmt_md.dumps(t)) must equal t. Any exception or difference is DEFECT. The line '- [ ] X #home !3 ^2026-01-01 (1)' has exactly the specified shape.

title: CSV dumps/loads cannot round-trip a valid task whose title contains NUL
spec_quote: `loads(dumps(tasks)) == tasks` for normalized tasks. (fmt_csv: "the `csv` module"; Python 3.9's csv reader rejects NUL, so a literal reading demands a workaround.)
probe_note: t = [normalize({id:1, title:'nul\x00x', created:'2026-01-01'})]; fmt_csv.loads(fmt_csv.dumps(t)) must equal t; an exception or difference is DEFECT. N/A if normalize itself rejects the title. strict_reading because the spec also mandates the csv module, whose 3.9 reader cannot read NUL; some implementations document the limit.

title: Saving resets an existing store file's permissions to 0600
spec_quote: Spec is silent on file permissions ("Every change is saved at once, through a temporary file in the same folder and `os.replace`").
probe_note: Write a valid empty store, chmod 0644, Store(path).add(...); mode must still be 0644. POSIX only (N/A elsewhere).

title: import saves once per task (and again for done tasks): a failing save leaves a partial import, a done task can stay open; quadratic run time
spec_quote: `import FORMAT FILE --today DATE` adds every task of the file as a new task (new ids, `created` = `today`, other fields kept) and prints how many. Spec is silent on atomicity and speed of import.
probe_note: Store with one task; run the CLI import of 3 jsonl tasks in a subprocess where os.replace (the mechanism the spec mandates) fails on its 2nd call. Afterwards the store must hold 1 task (nothing imported) or 4 (all imported in one save); any other count is DEFECT.

title: Markdown loads accepts extra spaces around the title
spec_quote: one line per task, `- [ ] TITLE` or `- [x] TITLE` (done), followed in this order by ... Lines that are empty are ignored on load; any other line that does not have this shape raises `TaskError`.
probe_note: fmt_md.loads must raise TaskError for '- [ ]  Buy !2 ^2026-01-01 (7)' and for '- [ ] Buy  !2 ^2026-01-01 (7)'; accepting either is DEFECT. strict_reading: whether a padded title still 'has this shape' is a literal reading.

title: Markdown loads accepts zero-padded priority or id
spec_quote: followed in this order by ... ` !PRIORITY`, ... ` (ID)`. ... any other line that does not have this shape raises `TaskError`.
probe_note: fmt_md.loads must raise TaskError for '- [ ] Buy !02 ^2026-01-01 (7)' and for '- [ ] Buy !2 ^2026-01-01 (007)'; accepting either is DEFECT.

title: Markdown loads accepts tags out of order or repeated
spec_quote: followed in this order by ` #TAG` for every tag ... any other line that does not have this shape raises `TaskError`. (Tags of a normalized task are de-duplicated and sorted.)
probe_note: fmt_md.loads must raise TaskError for '- [ ] Buy #b #a !2 ^2026-01-01 (7)' and for '- [ ] Buy #a #a !2 ^2026-01-01 (7)'; accepting either is DEFECT. strict_reading: one reviewer (r660acb1e) reads such a hand-written line as having the shape.

title: Markdown loads silently skips whitespace-only lines
spec_quote: Lines that are empty are ignored on load; any other line that does not have this shape raises `TaskError`.
probe_note: fmt_md.loads('   \n' + valid line) and fmt_md.loads('\t\n' + valid line) must raise TaskError; returning tasks is DEFECT. strict_reading: 'empty' versus 'blank' (the jsonl sentence says 'blank lines').

title: README tour shows the report command with no output
spec_quote: a README with a short tour. Spec is silent on its exact content.
probe_note: In README*, a line invoking `tasktrack ... report` that is directly followed by a closing code fence is DEFECT.

title: CLI numeric arguments accept non-ASCII digits (and _ separators, surrounding spaces)
spec_quote: bad arguments exit with status 2 and one line on stderr. Spec does not define the accepted digit syntax of ID / --priority N.
probe_note: `done \u0661` (Arabic-Indic one) on a store with task 1, and `add y --priority \u0662 --today 2026-01-01`; exit 0 for either is DEFECT.

title: CLI error message on stderr can contain line separators other than newline (U+2028, \x0b, \x1c from arguments)
spec_quote: exit with status 2 and one line on stderr, never a traceback. Spec does not define line separators beyond the newline; the message is one newline-terminated line.
probe_note: `add a 'b\u2028c\x0bd\x1ce' --today 2026-01-01` (an extra positional): stderr.decode().splitlines() must have exactly one element; more is DEFECT. N/A if the command does not exit 2.

title: report.render sorts tag keys itself instead of following the dict's key order
spec_quote: then `tag NAME: N` per tag in key order. Only differs for a by_tag dict not built by summary() (whose keys are sorted), i.e. input outside a valid summary.
probe_note: render({... by_tag: {'b': 1, 'a': 2}}) must list 'tag b: 1' before 'tag a: 2'; sorted output is DEFECT.

title: add accepts a title with undecodable bytes (lone surrogates); afterwards list fails for the whole store
spec_quote: Spec is silent on non-UTF-8 argv; exit 2 with one line holds.
probe_note: CLI `add b'bad\xff' --today 2026-01-01` (bytes argv); if add exits 0, a following default `list` must exit 0. add accepted and list failing is DEFECT. POSIX only.

title: Store changes the process-wide umask (os.umask(0) then restore) while saving
spec_quote: Spec is silent on umask handling.
probe_note: Subprocess wraps os.umask with a recording spy before importing tasktrack, then Store(new path).add + update; any os.umask call is DEFECT (each call changes the process umask, racing other threads).

title: Plain `python3 -m unittest` discovers no tests (tests/ is not a package)
spec_quote: tests with `unittest` under `tests/`. Spec does not fix the test command.
probe_note: In a subprocess, unittest.defaultTestLoader.discover('.') (what bare `python -m unittest` runs) must find at least one test; 0 is DEFECT.

title: `next ID RULE` fails unless a multi-word rule (every N days) is quoted
spec_quote: `next ID RULE` sets the task's due date to `next_due` of its current one. Spec is silent on shell quoting.
probe_note: Task 1 due 2026-01-05; `next 1 every 3 days` (unquoted, three argv words) must exit 0 and print 2026-01-08; anything else is DEFECT.

title: Store.get/remove do not accept the parameter name `id` the fixed interface names
spec_quote: The interface is fixed. ... `get(id) -> dict`, ... `remove(id)`
probe_note: s.get(id=1) must return task 1 and s.remove(id=2) must remove task 2; TypeError is DEFECT. update is not probed (a parameter named id would clash with update(1, id=5)). strict_reading: keyword use of the parameter name is a literal reading of the signature.

title: A code example in the docs/README is not valid Python (garbled normalize example in docs/model.md)
spec_quote: `docs/<module>.md` ... (what it does, its functions or commands, one example each). Another working example exists, so the deliverable is not missing.
probe_note: Compile every doctest example (>>>), every `python3 -c '...'` body and every ```python block without >>> in docs/*.md and README*; any SyntaxError is DEFECT.

title: Query parser rejects valid queries nested more than 100 levels (not/parentheses)
spec_quote: `parse(text) -> callable` returns a predicate over tasks; `TaskError` on a syntax error. ... An unknown field, a bad number or date, an unclosed parenthesis or quote, a missing operand and trailing tokens are syntax errors.
probe_note: parse('not '*150 + 'tag:x') and parse('('*150 + 'tag:x' + ')'*150) must return predicates that are true for a task tagged x; any exception or false is DEFECT. strict_reading: a depth guard is a common engineering limit.

title: Markdown dumps rejects (or loads splits) titles containing \x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, \x85, U+2028/2029
spec_quote: `loads(dumps(tasks)) == tasks` for normalized tasks. / Titles never contain ` #`, ` !`, ` @`, ` ^` or ` (` in this format: `dumps` raises `TaskError` for such a title.
probe_note: For each of \x0b \x0c \x1c \x1d \x1e \x85 \u2028 \u2029, t=[normalize({title:'a'+ch+'b',...})] must satisfy fmt_md.loads(fmt_md.dumps(t)) == t; any exception or difference is DEFECT. strict_reading: whether these count as line breaks in a one-line-per-task format is debatable.

title: Unclosed-parenthesis error message says 'at position' twice
spec_quote: Spec is silent on message wording ("an unclosed parenthesis ... [is a] syntax error").
probe_note: parse('(tag:a') raises TaskError; a message containing 'at position' more than once is DEFECT. N/A if no TaskError.

title: docs/query.md says whitespace between tokens is optional without the 'around parentheses and operators' restriction
spec_quote: whitespace between tokens optional around parentheses and operators. Docs wording only.
probe_note: In docs/query.md, a sentence (split at . or ;) that mentions 'whitespace' and 'optional' but none of parenthes/operator/around/only/except/word is DEFECT. N/A without docs/query.md.

title: Digit strings over 4300 characters end in a ValueError traceback (Python's int-conversion limit) instead of exit 2
spec_quote: Every `TaskError`, an unreadable file and bad arguments exit with status 2 and one line on stderr, never a traceback.
probe_note: CLI with a 5000-digit number: `list --query priority=N`, `import md` of a line with id (N), `import csv` with id N. Any 'Traceback' on stderr or exit code other than 0/2 is DEFECT. Python 3.9.6 has no int-string limit, so this shows only on newer interpreters (3.11+, and later 3.9/3.10 security releases).

title: Saving through a symlinked store path replaces the symlink with a regular file; the target is never updated
spec_quote: Spec is silent on symlinks ("through a temporary file in the same folder and `os.replace`").
probe_note: link.json -> real/t.json (valid empty store); Store(link).add(...); link must still be a symlink and the target must hold the task; otherwise DEFECT. POSIX only.

title: A newly created store file gets mode 0600 instead of following the umask
spec_quote: Spec is silent on file permissions.
probe_note: Subprocess with umask 022: Store(new path).add(...); the file mode must be 0644; otherwise DEFECT. POSIX only.

title: Missing library module (tasktrack/__init__, __main__, model, store, query, recur, fmt_jsonl, fmt_csv, fmt_md, report)
spec_quote: `tasktrack/model.py` ... `tasktrack/store.py` ... `tasktrack/query.py` ... `tasktrack/recur.py` ... `tasktrack/fmt_jsonl.py` ... `tasktrack/fmt_csv.py` ... `tasktrack/fmt_md.py` ... `tasktrack/report.py` ... (`python3 -m tasktrack --file PATH COMMAND …`)
probe_note: File-existence probe for each listed tasktrack/*.py (__main__.py is what `python -m tasktrack` needs). Any missing is DEFECT. No review reported it.

title: Missing docs file (docs/model, store, query, recur, formats, report, cli .md) or README
spec_quote: `docs/<module>.md` for `model`, `store`, `query`, `recur`, `formats`, `report` and `cli` ... and a README with a short tour.
probe_note: File-existence probe for the seven docs/*.md and any README* at the root. Any missing is DEFECT. No review reported it.

title: Missing per-module test file
spec_quote: `tests/test_<module>.py` per module.
probe_note: Requires tests/test_model, test_store, test_query, test_recur, test_report, a CLI test (test_cli or test_main/test___main__), and either all of test_fmt_jsonl/test_fmt_csv/test_fmt_md or test_formats. Any missing is DEFECT. No review reported it.
